turns.t: Mr. Alvarez, I have the letter from your clinic right here, from last week, so I know your readings had been climbing. Now tell me what's happened today.
I've been throwing up since last night, doctor, and my sugar's been through the roof all day. I'm scared, I can't keep anything down, not even water.
I'm his live-in carer. He started vomiting around eight last night, and by this morning he was so drowsy I didn't like it. That's when I called the ambulance.
You did exactly the right thing, thank you. Mr. Alvarez, how many times have you been sick?
I stopped counting. Maybe eight or nine times since last night. It's just a yellowish liquid now.
That's a lot, no wonder you feel wiped out. Have you taken your insulin as usual?
I took my long-acting insulin last night, 24 units, same as always. But I couldn't eat anything, so I wasn't sure if I should.
Okay. Is that the only medicine you take?
Yes, just that one.
Alright. Let me ask the nurse for your numbers. Nurse, what have we got?
Blood pressure is 98 over 60, heart rate is 118, and his blood sugar reading is 412.
Thank you. Have you got any chest pain, or trouble breathing?
No, my chest is fine. I'm breathing okay, just a bit fast, I guess.
Good. Let me have a look at you. Open your mouth for me.
Your mouth is very dry, the lining looks parched. Now I'll press on your belly, tell me if it hurts.
A bit sore up here, when you press. Not terrible.
Your belly is soft, with mild tenderness in the upper part. No sign of anything needing surgery, which is good.
Doctor, I already did a urine test when he came in, the result is on the screen.
Perfect, thanks. Mr. Alvarez, do you have any allergies we should know about before we give anything?
Hmm. I think so, maybe. There was some medicine they gave me in a hospital once that didn't agree with me. I couldn't tell you what it was.
I've only been with him two years, so I wouldn't know. It's not in his folder either.
Okay, we'll treat that as a possible allergy and be careful until we find out more. Is there anyone who could check old records?
My sister might know. I'll call her once I feel better.
Good idea. Now, here's what I'm thinking. With the vomiting, the high sugar, the fast breathing and the dry mouth, this looks like ketoacidosis, which means acid is building up in the blood.
Is that dangerous? Am I going to die?
It can be serious, but you've come in at a good time and we treat it every day. I want to be completely clear about what's next, and I won't leave you in the dark.
Okay. Thank you. Please just tell me what you're doing.
First, I'd like to order blood tests for ketones and your salts, to see how much acid and how low your fluids are.
Will it be another needle?
We can do it with a single stick, I promise.
And I'd also like to do an ECG, a heart tracing, because the salts can affect the heart's rhythm. It's painless, just stickers on your chest.
That's fine. Anything you need.
I'll decide on the treatment once the results are back. I'll come back to see you in two hours, or sooner if anything changes.
Can he have something to drink in the meantime?
Not for now, please. Nothing to eat or drink until I've seen the results, even sips, because he might vomit again.
All right. I'll stay right here with him.
Thank you, doctor. I feel safer already.
We've got you. Rest as best as you can.
